label: copy-phase input m, middle of the copy (recall_idx>=3, >=2 outputs left)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during the original or delimiter steps). About 96% of activation mass comes from steps where the fed-back input token is m, and m is never its first occurrence (the model is re-reading m that it copied). The strongest activations are when m was original token 2, so it is input at recall_idx 3 with 4-6 outputs still to go (top examples like l r m ... <DEL> l r [m]). It is near-silent for m early in the copy (recall_idx<=2) and weak or absent for m near the end of the copy (to_go 0-1). Small leftover activations show up on other copy-phase inputs, mostly 1, d, h, and p. Precision is limited because many mid-copy m inputs stay inactive or very weak, so position modulates the magnitude more than a hard cutoff can capture.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: m, 1, d, h, p, 0; least: t, e, v, n) and the previous input (most: r, i, h, l, m, p; least: e, v, w, <DEL>); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, t=12.
